statute_title: Operating a Motor Vehicle Under the Influence (DUI)
offense_class: Misdemeanor (first-third); Class D Felony (fourth+ within 10 years)
elements: Defendant operated or was in physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol, a controlled substance, or other substance that impairs driving
Or with a BAC of .08 or higher
Or while under the influence of a combination of alcohol and any substance
enhancements: Aggravating circumstances — BAC .15+, excessive speed (30+ over limit), wrong way, accident causing injury, minor in vehicle, refusal of test (doubled mandatory minimums)
Second offense within 10 years (increased penalties)
Fourth offense within 10 years (Class D Felony)
DUI causing death (separate charge under KRS § 507.050)
notes: Kentucky uses a 10-year lookback period. Aggravating circumstances double the mandatory minimum. Implied consent under KRS § 189A.103. License suspension 30-120 days (first), 12-18 months (second), 24-36 months (third), 60 months (fourth+). Ignition interlock required.

offense_class: Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle while under the influence
BAC .08 or higher or impairment shown
No prior DUI within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours imprisonment; alcohol/drug assessment; 90-day license suspension; fees and costs
enhancements: Aggravating circumstances double mandatory minimum to 96 hours
notes: First offense is a misdemeanor. Hardship license available after 30 days. Community service may substitute for jail time. DUI school required.

statute_title: DUI — Second, Third, or Subsequent Offense
offense_class: Misdemeanor (second/third within 10 years); Class D Felony (fourth+ within 10 years)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle while under the influence
Defendant has prior DUI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 7 days (second); 30 days (third); 120 days (fourth+); mandatory treatment; license revocation
enhancements: Aggravating circumstances double mandatory minimums
Fifth+ offense
notes: Fourth offense within 10 years is a Class D Felony. Kentucky allows treatment-based alternatives for some offenders. Mandatory alcohol/substance abuse treatment program.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated or was in physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of any other substance or combination of substances that impairs driving ability
Or while under combined influence of alcohol and any substance
enhancements: Same aggravating circumstances as alcohol DUI
notes: Kentucky does not have a per se drug DUI provision — prosecution must prove actual impairment. This differs from some states that criminalize any detectable amount.

offense_class: Violation (first); Misdemeanor (second+)
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle upon a highway
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
enhancements: Second or subsequent (Misdemeanor)
notes: First offense reckless driving is only a violation (non-criminal) in Kentucky — one of the least severe in the nation. Common plea-down from DUI.

statute_title: Leaving the Scene of an Accident
offense_class: Class D Felony (death or serious physical injury); Class A Misdemeanor (physical injury); Class B Misdemeanor (property only)
penalty_max: 5 years (Class D); 12 months (Class A); 90 days (Class B)
elements: Defendant was the operator of a vehicle involved in an accident
Resulting in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop, identify self, and render aid
enhancements: Death or serious physical injury (Class D Felony)
Physical injury (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Must stop immediately and provide name, address, and registration. Must render reasonable assistance to injured persons. Failure involving death is a Class D Felony.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant, under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
Wantonly engaged in conduct which created a grave risk of death
And thereby caused the death of another person
enhancements: DUI aggravator may support additional charges
notes: Kentucky charges DUI-related vehicular deaths as reckless homicide. Wanton murder (KRS § 507.020) may apply for more egregious cases. Manslaughter second degree (KRS § 507.040) is another option.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant wantonly caused the death of another person
Including but not limited to operation of a motor vehicle
notes: Second-degree manslaughter covers wanton killings without the extreme indifference required for murder. Often charged in DUI death cases as an alternative to reckless homicide.

statute_title: Operating on a Suspended or Revoked License
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Class D Felony (third+ or DUI-related suspension)
penalty_max: 90 days (Class B); 12 months (Class A); 5 years (Class D)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a public highway
While driving privileges were suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
enhancements: DUI-related suspension (mandatory jail)
Third or subsequent (Class D Felony)
notes: Driving on a DUI-suspended license carries mandatory jail time. Third offense is a felony. Notice of suspension creates presumption of knowledge.

offense_class: Class D Felony (motor vehicle); Class A Misdemeanor (on foot)
elements: Defendant, while operating a motor vehicle, fled or attempted to evade law enforcement
After being given a visual or audible signal to stop by a person recognized as a police officer
enhancements: Wanton endangerment during flight (additional charges)
Causing serious physical injury (Class C Felony under § 520.095(2))
Causing death (Class B Felony under § 520.095(3))
notes: Motor vehicle flight is automatically a Class D Felony. Serious injury during flight elevates to Class C. Death during flight is Class B. On-foot evasion is Class A Misdemeanor.

statute_title: Possession of a Controlled Substance — First Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully possessed a controlled substance
Classified in Schedule I or II (except marijuana)
Or a controlled substance analogue
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class D Felony, 1-5 years; Class C Felony, 5-10 years after second felony)
Proximity to school (additional penalty)
notes: Kentucky splits possession into first degree (Schedule I/II) and second degree (Schedule IV/V) and third degree (drug paraphernalia). First degree is a Class D Felony. Presumptive probation for first offense under HB 463.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (under 8 oz); Class A Misdemeanor (8 oz or more)
elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully possessed marijuana
enhancements: 8 ounces or more (Class A Misdemeanor)
5 or more plants (cultivation — Class D Felony under § 218A.1421)
notes: Kentucky has not legalized recreational marijuana. Simple possession under 8 oz is a Class B Misdemeanor. Possession of 8 oz or more is Class A. Cultivation of 5+ plants is a felony.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully possessed cocaine
enhancements: Second or subsequent drug felony (enhanced penalties)
Proximity to school
notes: Cocaine is Schedule II. Possession is a Class D Felony regardless of amount. HB 463 presumptive probation may apply for first offense.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully possessed methamphetamine
enhancements: 2 grams or more (Trafficking charge possible under § 218A.1412)
Prior drug felony
notes: Meth possession is a Class D Felony. Kentucky has significant meth enforcement. Possession of 2 grams or more creates presumption of trafficking. HB 463 presumptive probation for first offense.

statute_title: Trafficking in a Controlled Substance — First Degree
offense_class: Class C Felony (first); Class B Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully trafficked in a controlled substance classified in Schedule I or II
Trafficking includes manufacturing, distributing, dispensing, selling, or possessing with intent to distribute
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class B Felony)
Aggravating factors — near school, to minor, large quantity
Causing death by distribution (enhanced)
notes: First-degree trafficking covers Schedule I and II substances. Weight thresholds vary by substance — for cocaine, 4 grams or more; for meth, 2 grams or more. Not eligible for probation without court finding of extraordinary circumstances.

statute_title: Trafficking in a Controlled Substance — Second Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony (first); Class C Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully trafficked in a controlled substance classified in Schedule III, IV, or V
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class C Felony)
notes: Second-degree trafficking covers lower schedule substances. Less severe than first-degree trafficking.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured or attempted to manufacture methamphetamine
enhancements: Causing serious physical injury (Class A Felony)
Causing death (Class A Felony, 20-50 years or life)
Manufacture in presence of a minor (enhanced)
notes: Kentucky's separate meth manufacturing statute carries significantly harsher penalties than general trafficking. Class B Felony — 10-20 years. Environmental cleanup costs may be assessed.

statute_title: Use or Possession of Drug Paraphernalia
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant used or possessed with intent to use drug paraphernalia
To introduce into the human body a controlled substance
enhancements: Delivery to a minor (Class D Felony under § 218A.500(3))
notes: Use or possession is a Class A Misdemeanor. Sale of paraphernalia is a Class A Misdemeanor. Delivery to a minor is a Class D Felony.

statute_title: Possession with Intent to Distribute — First Degree
offense_class: Class C Felony (first); Class B Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance (Schedule I or II)
With intent to manufacture, sell, or distribute
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class B Felony)
Near school property
Distribution to minor
notes: Intent is inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, and other circumstantial evidence. Charged under the trafficking statute.

offense_class: Capital Offense or Class A Felony
penalty_min: 20 years (Class A); death or life without parole (capital)
penalty_max: 50 years or life without parole (Class A); death (capital)
elements: Defendant, with intent to cause the death of another person, caused the death of that person or a third person
Including situations where the person wantonly engages in conduct creating a grave risk of death under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
mandatory_minimum: 20 years before parole eligibility (without aggravating factors); death or life without parole (with aggravating factors)
enhancements: Aggravating factors for capital sentencing (KRS § 532.025)
notes: Kentucky has a single murder statute covering both intentional killing and wanton murder (extreme indifference). Kentucky retains the death penalty. Murder is not split into 'degrees' — instead, severity ranges from Class A to capital based on aggravating factors.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant wantonly engaged in conduct which created a grave risk of death to another person
Under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
And thereby caused the death of another person
notes: Wanton murder is the functional equivalent of second-degree murder in Kentucky. Same statute as intentional murder but under the 'wanton/extreme indifference' prong. Class A Felony with 20-50 years or LWOP.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant, with intent to cause the death of another person, caused the death of that person
Under the influence of extreme emotional disturbance for which there was a reasonable explanation
notes: Kentucky uses 'extreme emotional disturbance' (EED) rather than 'heat of passion.' EED is a partial defense that reduces murder to first-degree manslaughter. Defendant bears the burden of production on EED.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant wantonly caused the death of another person
Including but not limited to situations involving reckless operation of a motor vehicle
notes: Second-degree manslaughter is the wanton (not intentional) killing of another person — equivalent to involuntary manslaughter in other states. Common in vehicular death cases.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally caused serious physical injury to another person by means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
Or wantonly engaged in conduct which created a grave risk of death and caused serious physical injury
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (element of the offense)
notes: First-degree assault is the most serious non-homicide violent offense. Class B Felony — 10-20 years. Requires serious physical injury (risk of death, extreme physical pain, protracted impairment).

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally or wantonly caused physical injury to another person
Or recklessly caused physical injury by means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
enhancements: Against certain protected persons — school employees, social workers, corrections officers (Class D Felony)
notes: Fourth-degree assault is Kentucky's simple assault/battery. 'Physical injury' means substantial physical pain or visible physical injury. Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly caused serious physical injury to another person by means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
Or intentionally caused or attempted to cause physical injury to certain protected persons
enhancements: Against police, firefighter, EMT, or corrections officer (Class D Felony)
notes: Third-degree assault is a Class D Felony. Bridges the gap between simple assault (misdemeanor) and first-degree assault (Class B Felony). Often charged when serious injury results from reckless conduct.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant took property from another person or in the presence of another person
By the use or threatened use of physical force
enhancements: Use of deadly weapon or serious physical injury (First Degree — Class B Felony)
notes: Second-degree robbery is the base robbery charge — force or threat of force without a weapon. Class C Felony, 5-10 years.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant committed robbery
While armed with a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
Or caused serious physical injury to a non-participant
enhancements: Violent offender provision (KRS § 439.3401) — must serve 85% of sentence
notes: First-degree robbery is a Class B violent felony. Subject to violent offender provision — 85% of sentence must be served before parole eligibility.

offense_class: Class B Felony; Class A Felony (serious physical injury or ransom)
penalty_max: 20 years (Class B); 50 years or LWOP (Class A)
elements: Defendant unlawfully restrained another person
And moved or confined the person with intent to hold for ransom, facilitate a felony, inflict injury, terrorize, or interfere with government function
enhancements: Serious physical injury (Class A Felony)
Ransom demand (Class A Felony)
notes: Kidnapping requires unlawful restraint plus movement or confinement with specified intent. Unlawful imprisonment (§ 509.020) is a lesser included offense requiring only restraint.

offense_class: Class A Felony (first degree — building with persons); Class B Felony (second — occupied building); Class C Felony (third — building)
penalty_min: 20 years (Class A); 10 years (Class B); 5 years (Class C)
penalty_max: 50 years or LWOP (Class A); 20 years (Class B); 10 years (Class C)
elements: Defendant started a fire or caused an explosion with intent to destroy or damage a building
First degree: building in which a person was present
Second degree: building that is the dwelling of another
enhancements: Person present in building (First Degree — Class A Felony)
Dwelling (Second Degree — Class B Felony)
notes: First-degree arson with persons present is Class A Felony — among the most serious charges in Kentucky. Three degrees based on building type and occupancy.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant, with intent to commit murder
Engaged in conduct which constituted a substantial step toward the commission of murder
enhancements: Violent offender provision — 85% of sentence before parole
notes: Criminal attempt of a capital offense is a Class B Felony under KRS § 506.010. Subject to violent offender statute — 85% must be served.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally caused physical injury to another person by means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
Or wantonly caused serious physical injury by means of a deadly weapon
enhancements: Serious physical injury — may elevate to first-degree assault (Class B Felony)
notes: Second-degree assault fills the gap between first-degree (serious injury with weapon) and fourth-degree (simple assault). Class C Felony — 5-10 years.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $500); Class D Felony ($500-$9,999); Class C Felony ($10,000+)
penalty_max: 12 months (Class A); 5 years (Class D); 10 years (Class C)
elements: Defendant unlawfully took or exercised control over movable property of another
With intent to deprive the owner thereof
enhancements: Value $500+ (Class D Felony)
Value $10,000+ (Class C Felony)
Theft of a firearm (Class D Felony regardless of value)
notes: Kentucky's felony theft threshold is $500 — among the lowest in the nation. Theft of a firearm is automatically a Class D Felony.

statute_title: Theft by Unlawful Taking — $500 or More
offense_class: Class D Felony ($500-$9,999); Class C Felony ($10,000+)
elements: Defendant unlawfully took property of another
With intent to deprive
Value $500 or more
enhancements: Value $10,000+ (Class C Felony)
notes: Kentucky does not use 'grand theft' terminology. Felony theft based on $500 threshold — very low compared to national averages.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant unlawfully took property of another
With intent to deprive
Value under $500
enhancements: Prior theft convictions may enhance
notes: Misdemeanor theft for property valued under $500. Diversion programs available in some jurisdictions for first offenders.

statute_title: Theft by Unlawful Taking — Retail Theft (Shoplifting)
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $500); Class D Felony ($500+)
elements: Defendant unlawfully took merchandise from a retail establishment
With intent to deprive the retailer
enhancements: Value $500+ (Class D Felony)
Organized retail theft
notes: Shoplifting is charged under the general theft statute. $500 felony threshold. Retailers may pursue civil recovery.

offense_class: Class C Felony (second degree — building); Class B Felony (first degree — dwelling with person present)
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully in a building
With intent to commit a crime therein
enhancements: Dwelling with person present (First Degree — Class B Felony)
Armed with a deadly weapon or explosive (First Degree)
Causing physical injury (First Degree)
notes: Second-degree burglary is entry into any building. First-degree is dwelling while person present, or entry with weapon/injury. Third degree (§ 511.040) covers non-building structures.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully in a dwelling
With intent to commit a crime
While another person was present
Or while armed with a deadly weapon or causing physical injury
enhancements: Violent offender provision — 85% of sentence before parole
notes: First-degree burglary is a Class B violent felony. Subject to violent offender statute — 85% must be served. Requires either a person present, a weapon, or injury.

offense_class: Class D Felony (most vehicles exceed $500 threshold); Class C Felony ($10,000+)
elements: Defendant unlawfully took or exercised control over a motor vehicle of another
With intent to deprive the owner
enhancements: Vehicle value over $10,000 (Class C Felony)
notes: Motor vehicle theft follows the general theft statute. Most vehicles exceed the $500 felony threshold. Unauthorized use of a vehicle (§ 514.100) is a lesser charge.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $500); Class D Felony ($500-$9,999); Class C Felony ($10,000+)
penalty_max: 12 months (Class A); 5 years (Class D); 10 years (Class C)
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of movable property of another
Knowing or believing it was stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
enhancements: Same value tiers as theft
notes: Separate statute from theft but same value thresholds apply. 'Knowing or believing' standard — actual knowledge not strictly required.

statute_title: Criminal Mischief in the First Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony ($1,000+); Class A Misdemeanor ($500-$999); Class B Misdemeanor (under $500)
penalty_max: 5 years (Class D); 12 months (Class A); 90 days (Class B)
elements: Defendant intentionally or wantonly destroyed or damaged the property of another
enhancements: Damage $1,000+ (Class D Felony)
notes: Three degrees of criminal mischief in Kentucky based on damage amount and intent. First degree ($1,000+) is a Class D Felony. Restitution typically ordered.

statute_title: Criminal Trespass in the Third Degree
offense_class: Violation; Class A Misdemeanor (first degree — dwelling)
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully in or upon the premises of another
After notice from owner or agent
enhancements: Building (Second Degree — Class B Misdemeanor)
Dwelling (First Degree — Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Three degrees: third degree (premises), second degree (building), first degree (dwelling). Notice can be posted signs, fencing, or verbal notice.

offense_class: Same as vandalism entry
elements: Defendant intentionally or wantonly destroyed or damaged the property of another
enhancements: Same as vandalism entry
notes: Criminal mischief is Kentucky's statutory term for vandalism/property destruction. Three degrees based on damage amount.

statute_title: Assault in the Fourth Degree — Domestic Violence
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (third+ within 5 years or strangulation)
elements: Defendant intentionally or wantonly caused physical injury to a family member or member of an unmarried couple
As defined in KRS § 403.720
enhancements: Third or subsequent within 5 years (Class D Felony under § 508.032)
Strangulation (Class D Felony under § 508.032(2))
notes: Kentucky has a specific domestic violence assault statute. Strangulation was elevated to a felony in recent legislation. Mandatory arrest. Emergency protective order automatically issued.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (enhanced)
elements: Defendant intentionally caused physical injury to a family member or member of an unmarried couple
Or made physical contact of an insulting or provoking nature
enhancements: Third offense within 5 years (Class D Felony)
Strangulation (Class D Felony)
notes: Same statute as domestic violence entry. Federal firearms prohibition upon conviction (18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(9)). 'Family member or member of an unmarried couple' includes co-parents and persons in dating relationships.

statute_title: Endangering the Welfare of a Minor
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (if involving custody violation or serious risk)
elements: Defendant knowingly failed to provide adequate food, clothing, shelter, education, or medical care to a minor
Or placed a minor in a situation which endangered the minor's life or health
enhancements: Resulting in serious physical injury (additional assault charges)
Drug exposure
notes: Covers neglect and reckless endangerment of children. Cabinet for Health and Family Services (CHFS) investigates. Criminal charges and dependency proceedings may run in parallel.

statute_title: Criminal Abuse in the First Degree
offense_class: Class C Felony (first degree — serious physical injury); Class D Felony (second degree — physical injury)
elements: Defendant intentionally abused a person 12 or under, or a person who is physically helpless or mentally helpless
And the abuse resulted in serious physical injury
enhancements: Serious physical injury (First Degree — Class C Felony)
notes: Kentucky's criminal abuse statute covers abuse of children under 12 and vulnerable adults. First degree requires serious physical injury. Second degree (§ 508.110) covers abuse causing physical injury or risk.

statute_title: Violation of a Domestic Violence Order (DVO)
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (with physical injury, third+ offense, or possession of weapon during violation)
elements: A domestic violence order (DVO) or emergency protective order (EPO) was issued
Defendant intentionally violated the order
enhancements: Physical injury to protected person (Class D Felony)
Third or subsequent violation (Class D Felony)
Possession of a weapon during violation (Class D Felony)
notes: Kentucky takes DVO violations seriously. Felony charges apply for injury, weapons, or repeat violations. Mandatory arrest when officer has probable cause.

offense_class: Class D Felony (first degree — explicit/implicit threat); Class A Misdemeanor (second degree — pattern without threat)
elements: Defendant intentionally stalked another person
Made an explicit or implicit threat with intent to place person in reasonable fear of sexual contact, physical injury, or death
Or engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized
enhancements: Threat of violence (First Degree — Class D Felony)
Protective order in effect (enhanced)
notes: First-degree stalking requires an explicit or implicit threat. Second-degree covers harassment patterns without direct threats. Cyberstalking included.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (physical contact or against specific officials)
elements: Defendant, with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm another person
Subjected that person to physical contact, or threatened to do so
Or made repeated unwanted communications
enhancements: Physical contact (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Harassment covers unwanted communications, following, and minor physical contact. More serious conduct may be charged as stalking or assault.

statute_title: Criminal Abuse — Physically Helpless or Mentally Helpless Person
offense_class: Class C Felony (first degree); Class D Felony (second degree)
elements: Defendant intentionally abused a person who is physically helpless or mentally helpless
Causing serious physical injury (first degree) or physical injury or risk thereof (second degree)
enhancements: Serious physical injury (Class C Felony)
notes: Kentucky charges elder abuse under the criminal abuse statute. Financial exploitation is covered under KRS § 209.990. Adult Protective Services investigates.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed deadly weapon on or about the person
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
notes: Kentucky enacted permitless concealed carry (constitutional carry) in 2019 for persons 21 and older. This statute now primarily applies to prohibited persons and persons under 21.

statute_title: Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon
offense_class: Class D Felony; Class C Felony (violent felony prior)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed, manufactured, or transported a firearm
Defendant has been convicted of a felony
enhancements: Prior violent felony (Class C Felony)
notes: Applies to all convicted felons. Prior violent felony elevates to Class C Felony. Federal charges (18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1)) may also apply.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (prohibited person or second+)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed deadly weapon
Defendant is a prohibited person (under 21, felon, or subject of DVO)
notes: With 2019 constitutional carry, this primarily applies to prohibited persons. Persons subject to active domestic violence orders are prohibited from carrying.

offense_class: Class D Felony (at occupied dwelling/vehicle); Class A Misdemeanor (other)
elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
At or into a dwelling, building, or occupied vehicle
Under circumstances which create a risk of physical injury
enhancements: At occupied dwelling or vehicle (Class D Felony)
notes: Discharging at an occupied structure is a Class D Felony. General reckless discharge may also be charged as wanton endangerment under § 508.060.

offense_class: Class D Felony; Class C Felony ($500+ loss)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed or used the personal identifying information of another person
Without authorization
With intent to represent that the defendant is the other person for the purpose of committing fraud
enhancements: Loss $500+ (Class C Felony)
Victim over 60 or disabled (Class C Felony)
notes: Kentucky identity theft statute covers SSN, driver's license numbers, bank account numbers, and other personal identifiers. Restitution typically ordered.

statute_title: Theft by Failure to Make Required Disposition of Property (Embezzlement)
offense_class: Same as theft by value — Class A Misdemeanor to Class C Felony
elements: Defendant obtained property of another upon agreement or known legal obligation to make specified payment or disposition
Defendant intentionally dealt with the property in a manner inconsistent with the agreement or obligation
enhancements: Same value tiers as theft
notes: Kentucky has a separate embezzlement statute within the consolidated theft chapter. Same penalty structure as general theft based on value.

offense_class: Class C Felony (first degree — money/securities/government); Class D Felony (second degree — deeds/wills/contracts)
elements: Defendant, with intent to defraud, deceive, or injure another
Falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
First degree: money, stamps, securities, or government documents
enhancements: Government documents or money (First Degree — Class C Felony)
notes: Three degrees of forgery in Kentucky. First degree covers money and government instruments (Class C). Second degree covers deeds, wills, and commercial instruments (Class D). Third degree covers other documents (Class A Misdemeanor).

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant falsely made, completed, or altered currency or government instruments
With intent to defraud
notes: Counterfeiting is charged as first-degree forgery in Kentucky. Primarily a federal offense but state charges may apply.

offense_class: Same as theft by value — Class A Misdemeanor to Class C Felony
elements: Defendant issued a check knowing there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
In exchange for property, services, or anything of value
enhancements: Same value tiers as theft
notes: Cold check offenses follow the theft by deception statute. Separate cold check complaint procedures exist under KRS § 514.040. 10-day notice before prosecution.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly presented or caused to be presented a false or fraudulent claim for insurance benefits
Or knowingly prepared false documentation to support a claim
notes: Kentucky Department of Insurance investigates. Restitution and civil penalties in addition to criminal penalties.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit Card
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $500); Class D Felony ($500+)
elements: Defendant used a credit card knowing it was stolen, forged, revoked, or expired
Or used another's card without authorization
To obtain money, goods, or services
enhancements: Amount $500+ (Class D Felony)
notes: Kentucky has specific credit card fraud statutes within the commercial fraud chapter. May also be charged as identity theft or theft by deception.

statute_title: Money Laundering — Use of Proceeds from Controlled Substance Trafficking
offense_class: Class C Felony
fine_max: $10,000 or twice the value of the property involved, whichever is greater
elements: Defendant knowingly conducted a financial transaction involving proceeds derived from trafficking in controlled substances
With intent to promote trafficking or to conceal the nature/source of the proceeds
notes: Kentucky's money laundering statute is located in the controlled substances chapter. Covers proceeds from drug trafficking. Forfeiture provisions under KRS § 218A.410 also apply.

offense_class: Same as theft by value
elements: Defendant obtained property of another by creating or reinforcing a false impression
As to value, intention, or other material fact
With intent to deprive the owner
enhancements: Same value tiers as theft
notes: Theft by deception is Kentucky's general fraud statute within the consolidated theft chapter. Covers false representations, bait-and-switch, and con schemes.

statute_title: Sexual Abuse in the First Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant subjected another person to sexual contact by forcible compulsion
Or the person was incapable of consent due to physical helplessness or mental incapacity
enhancements: Victim under 12 (enhanced — typically charged as first-degree sexual abuse of a minor)
notes: Sexual abuse in the first degree is Kentucky's term for sexual assault involving forcible compulsion or incapacity. Class D Felony. Sex offender registration required.

offense_class: Class B Felony; Class A Felony (serious physical injury or victim under 12)
penalty_max: 20 years (Class B); 50 years or LWOP (Class A)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse with another person by forcible compulsion
Or the person was incapable of consent due to physical helplessness or being less than 12 years old
mandatory_minimum: Violent offender statute — 85% of sentence before parole
enhancements: Serious physical injury (Class A Felony)
Victim under 12 (Class A Felony)
notes: Rape first degree is a Class B violent felony — 85% must be served. Rape involving serious injury or victim under 12 is Class A Felony. Sex offender registration is lifetime.

statute_title: Indecent Exposure in the First Degree
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (second degree); Class A Misdemeanor (first degree — to minor); Class D Felony (second+ or registered sex offender)
penalty_max: 90 days (Class B); 12 months (Class A); 5 years (Class D)
elements: Defendant intentionally exposed the person's genitals under circumstances in which the conduct is likely to be seen by others
First degree: directed toward a minor under 18 or by a registered sex offender
enhancements: Exposure to minor (First Degree — Class A Misdemeanor or Class D Felony)
Registered sex offender (Class D Felony)
notes: Two degrees of indecent exposure. Second degree is general exposure. First degree involves minors or sex offender status. Second+ offense of first degree is a Class D Felony.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second+); Class D Felony (patronizing minor)
penalty_max: 90 days (Class B); 12 months (Class A); 5 years (Class D)
elements: Defendant engaged in or offered to engage in sexual conduct for a fee
Or agreed to pay a fee for sexual conduct
enhancements: Second or subsequent (Class A Misdemeanor)
Patronizing a minor (Class D Felony under § 529.040)
notes: Base prostitution is a Class B Misdemeanor. Promoting prostitution (§ 529.040) is a Class D Felony. Human trafficking charges (§ 529.100) apply when force, fraud, or coercion is involved.

statute_title: Possession or Viewing of Matter Portraying a Sexual Performance by a Minor
offense_class: Class D Felony (first); Class C Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed or viewed material portraying a sexual performance by a minor
enhancements: Distribution (Class C Felony under § 531.340)
Production (Class B Felony under § 531.310)
Second or subsequent possession (Class C Felony)
notes: Each image/video is a separate count. Production is Class B Felony. Distribution is Class C Felony. Sex offender registration required for all offenses.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant is required to register under the Kentucky Sex Offender Registry
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update registration
notes: Must register within 5 business days of establishing residence. Must verify every 90 days (sexually violent predators) or annually (others). Each day of failure may constitute a separate offense.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant, being 21 or older, engaged in sexual intercourse with a person under 16
Or being any age, engaged in sexual intercourse with a person under 14
enhancements: Victim under 12 (First Degree Rape — Class B or A Felony)
notes: Kentucky's age of consent is 16. Rape third degree covers consensual intercourse where the victim is under age. Penalty increases significantly for victims under 12.

statute_title: Disorderly Conduct in the Second Degree
offense_class: Violation (second degree); Class B Misdemeanor (first degree)
elements: Defendant, with intent to cause public inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm
Or recklessly creating a risk thereof
Engaged in fighting, made unreasonable noise, or created a hazardous condition
enhancements: First degree (Class B Misdemeanor) — in a public place where 10 or more people are gathered
notes: Second-degree disorderly conduct is only a violation (non-criminal). First degree requires a gathering of 10+ people. Common charge for bar fights and public disturbances.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally prevented or attempted to prevent a peace officer
Known or reasonably known to be a peace officer
From effecting an arrest by using or threatening physical force
enhancements: Causing physical injury to officer (additional assault charges)
notes: Resisting arrest is a Class A Misdemeanor in Kentucky. Does not require the underlying arrest to be lawful — lawfulness of arrest is not a defense. Passive resistance may not be sufficient.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant, by using or threatening physical force
Intentionally obstructed, impaired, or perverted the administration of law or government function
notes: General obstruction statute. Covers evidence tampering and witness intimidation under separate statutes (KRS §§ 524.040, 524.050). Tampering with physical evidence is a Class D Felony.

offense_class: Court-imposed sanctions
penalty_max: 6 months for criminal contempt; indefinite for civil contempt until compliance
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed or violated a court order
Or disrupted court proceedings
Or refused to comply with a lawful court directive
notes: Kentucky distinguishes criminal contempt (punitive) from civil contempt (coercive). Direct contempt may be punished summarily. Indirect contempt requires notice and hearing.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first/second); Class A Misdemeanor (third+ within 12 months)
elements: Defendant appeared in a public place under the influence of alcohol
Or any other substance to the degree that the person was a danger to self or others
Or was manifestly under the influence to the degree that the person unreasonably annoyed others
enhancements: Third or subsequent within 12 months (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Kentucky calls this 'alcohol intoxication' rather than public intoxication. Must be a danger to self/others or manifestly annoying. Officers may transport to a treatment facility instead of jail.

statute_title: Bail Jumping in the First Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony (felony case); Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor case under § 520.080)
elements: Defendant, while released on bail or recognizance
Intentionally failed to appear as required
With intent to evade or delay the judicial process
enhancements: Underlying felony case (Class D Felony — bail jumping first degree)
notes: Bail jumping first degree (felony case) is a Class D Felony. Bail jumping second degree (misdemeanor case) is Class A Misdemeanor. Bond forfeiture and bench warrant issued.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class B Misdemeanor (false alarm)
elements: Defendant gave false information to a law enforcement officer
Or made a false report of a crime or emergency
Knowing the report to be false
notes: False police reports and false emergency calls. Swatting may lead to additional charges if harm results.

statute_title: Terroristic Threatening in the First Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony (first degree); Class A Misdemeanor (third degree under § 508.080(2))
elements: Defendant threatened to commit any crime likely to result in death or serious physical injury
Or to cause serious disruption to public services or transportation
The threat placed persons in fear
notes: Terroristic threatening first degree is a Class D Felony. Third degree (general threats causing alarm) is a Class A Misdemeanor. Bomb threats to schools are first degree.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant made a material false statement under oath
In an official proceeding
Knowing it to be false
notes: First-degree perjury requires the statement be in an official proceeding. Second-degree perjury (Class A Misdemeanor) covers sworn written statements.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer any benefit upon a public servant
With intent to influence the public servant's vote, opinion, judgment, or action
notes: Class C Felony — Kentucky treats public corruption seriously. Both the giver and receiver of a bribe may be charged.

offense_class: Class C Felony (first degree — from custody on felony); Class D Felony (second degree — from custody on misdemeanor); Class A Misdemeanor (third degree — from protective custody)
penalty_max: 10 years (Class C); 5 years (Class D); 12 months (Class A)
elements: Defendant escaped from custody or a detention facility
While held on a criminal charge or conviction
enhancements: Use of force or weapon (enhanced)
notes: Three degrees based on the underlying custody. First degree (felony custody) is Class C Felony. Includes walking away from work release or home incarceration.

statute_title: Cruelty to Animals in the First Degree
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (second+ or torture causing death); Class C Felony (dogfighting)
penalty_max: 12 months (Class A); 5 years (Class D); 10 years (Class C)
elements: Defendant intentionally caused or permitted the torture, mutilation, or death of an animal
Or subjected an animal to cruel mistreatment
enhancements: Torture causing serious physical injury or death (Class D Felony)
Second or subsequent (Class D Felony)
Dogfighting (Class C Felony under § 525.125(2))
notes: Kentucky strengthened animal cruelty laws. First offense animal torture causing serious injury or death is a Class D Felony. Dogfighting is a Class C Felony.

offense_class: Not a new criminal charge — court may revoke probation and impose original sentence
penalty_max: Up to the maximum sentence for the original offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation or conditional discharge
Defendant violated a condition of supervision
Violation proven by preponderance of the evidence
notes: Kentucky uses graduated sanctions for probation violations. Court may continue, modify, or revoke probation. New criminal conduct typically results in revocation.

offense_class: Not a new criminal charge — Parole Board determines consequences
penalty_max: Return to incarceration for remainder of sentence
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
notes: Kentucky Parole Board conducts revocation hearings. Parolee has right to counsel. Graduated sanctions available for technical violations.

statute_title: Liability for Conduct of Another — Complicity
offense_class: Same as the underlying offense
elements: Defendant, acting with the kind of culpability sufficient for the commission of the offense
Solicited, counseled, commanded, or intentionally aided another to commit the offense
notes: Kentucky uses 'complicity' rather than 'aiding and abetting.' A person is legally accountable for the conduct of another. Mere presence is insufficient — must show active participation.

offense_class: One class below the underlying offense (Class B for capital/Class A offenses; Class C for Class B; Class D for Class C; Class A Misdemeanor for Class D)
penalty_max: One class below the completed offense
elements: Defendant, with intent to commit a specific crime
Engaged in conduct which constituted a substantial step toward the commission of the crime
notes: Attempt is graded one class below the completed offense. Attempted murder (capital/Class A) is a Class B Felony. Renunciation is a defense if complete and voluntary.

offense_class: One class below the target offense
penalty_max: Same as attempt — one class below the target
elements: Defendant, with intent to promote or facilitate the commission of a crime
Agreed with one or more persons to engage in or cause conduct constituting a crime
Defendant or co-conspirator performed an overt act in furtherance of the conspiracy
notes: Conspiracy requires agreement, intent, and an overt act. Graded one class below the target offense. Renunciation is a defense if the defendant notified co-conspirators and law enforcement.
